forced_trigger.S06_evidence: v4 receives EasyEnsemble as an additional candidate; the Arbiter chooses it in 533/600 cases. This shows behavior when a dominant candidate is almost always selected.
forced_trigger.concept: What if the adaptation is always triggered (ignore IR gate)?

gb_only.S06_evidence: v1 behaves mostly as a comparison between GB and SMOTE; the actual selection distribution is documented in S06 analysis. When the Arbiter selects GB, its mean delta is reported in the S06c finding.
gb_only.concept: What if only GradientBoosting is available?

no_arbiter.S06_evidence: v1 uses one candidate (GB or SMOTE) chosen by utility; S06c v4 forces the Arbiter to see EasyEnsemble as one candidate. The comparison of v1/v2/v3/v4 effectively covers the effect of changing the Arbiter rule.
no_arbiter.concept: What if the Arbiter is bypassed?

smote_only.S06_evidence: The counterfactual in S05 (always-SMOTE+RF) computes exactly this comparison and is fully documented in S05/analysis/counterfactual_arbiter.json.
smote_only.concept: What if only SMOTE+RF is available?
